title: The desalination energy cost floor
bottleneck: Reverse osmosis is approaching its thermodynamic limit — modern plants use about 3 kWh per cubic meter against a theoretical minimum near 1 kWh — which means future cost reductions must come from cheaper energy, not better membranes. Desalination already consumes up to 10x the energy of conventional water treatment, and scaling it to water-scarce regions means scaling energy demand that poor grids can't meet.
why_it_blocks: Water scarcity affects billions, but desalination can't serve them if each cubic meter requires energy they don't have. The energy floor caps how cheap desalinated water can ever get.
current_state: Sorek B set record-low contracted prices and next-gen membranes promise sub-2 kWh per cubic meter in pilots, but the thermodynamic wall is fixed.
